skills.name: agent-guardrails
skills.description: Turn recurring agent mistakes in a project into enforceable constraints. Use when the user keeps correcting the same mistake or asks to prevent a repeated class of errors. Do NOT use for a single bug fix, general code review, or skill-library cleanup.

skills.name: benchmark-checklist
skills.description: Check whether a measured performance claim supports a comparison or decision. Use when running benchmarks, reporting a measured speedup or regression, or choosing between implementations from timing results. Do NOT use for interpreting published benchmarks without running them or for general debugging.

skills.name: blast-radius
skills.description: Trace what a change could break beyond its diff and verify the assumptions its safety depends on. Use for "blast radius", "what could this break", or indirect compatibility and lifecycle risks. Use code-review for a general diff review.

skills.name: blog-review
skills.description: Review a technical blog draft and report what loses its reader, ordered by cost. Use when asked to review, critique, give feedback on, or tighten a draft blog post, article, newsletter issue, or engineering essay, or to 审稿 / 看看这篇. Do NOT use for READMEs, guides, comments, or commit text (use write-docs), for design docs, or to write a post from scratch.

skills.name: code-review
skills.description: Review a diff, package, or API through one of five lenses — necessity and layering (Russ Cox), honest invariants and costs (BurntSushi), product-versus-library fit (Mitsuhiko), a complexity gate before a design change, or newcomer clarity. Use when asked to review, audit, or polish code, vet a dependency, judge whether a change is too complex, or find what a new hire would not understand.

skills.name: create-formal-verification-skill
skills.description: Generates a project-local skill that formally verifies the code where a bug costs the most and tests reach the least, in any language, with whichever verification tool fits. Use for /create-formal-verification-skill, "verify this subsystem", or when concurrency, retries, state machines, parsers, or unsafe code need more than tests. Do NOT use for one ad hoc TLA+ spec (use tla-model) or to drive a running app for evidence (use create-verification-skill).

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.description: Create a project-local skill for launching, driving, and collecting evidence from a real app, CLI, API, or library. Use when asked to create a reusable verification workflow or control skill for a project. Do NOT use for a one-off smoke check, ordinary unit-test writing, or formal verification of a design or invariant (use create-formal-verification-skill).

skills.name: dataviz
skills.description: Design and implement evidence-first charts from real data for technical blogs, reports, READMEs, and product explainers. Use when asked for a benchmark graph, data illustration, performance chart, tradeoff plot, small multiple, or an editorial chart in React/Recharts or a static plotting stack. Do NOT use for text-only diagrams (use show-me), hand-drawn conceptual art (use sketch-concept), or dashboard UI design.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.description: Keeps a project's vocabulary and decision records honest by challenging overloaded terms against the code and recording canonical terms and hard-to-reverse decisions where the repo already keeps them. Use when a term, status, or field means two things, when naming a new concept or state, or when editing a glossary, GLOSSARY.md, or ADR. Do NOT use to interview the user about a plan (use grill-me) or to write a design doc.

skills.name: grill-me
skills.description: Resolves the open decisions of a plan or design with the user in short rounds of numbered questions, each with its context, options, and a recommended answer. Use when asked to "grill me" or stress-test a design, or when a plan has two or more open decisions only the user can make, including from karpathy-planning, state-prototype, or domain-modeling. Do NOT use for one quick clarifying question, or to collect comments on a long document (use readback).

skills.name: grok-repo
skills.description: Explain an unfamiliar codebase through a repository briefing, dataflow trace, or reconstruction of why and how a change was made. Use when asked for a repo tour, design tradeoffs, how something works, where a value comes from, or why a feature changed. Not for repo health (use repo-eval).

skills.name: hammerspoon
skills.description: Operate macOS via Hammerspoon, either one-off `hs -c` Lua (launch, quit, or focus apps and browser tabs; volume, wifi, caffeinate, alerts, clipboard) or persistent hotkeys, watchers, and menubar items in ~/.hammerspoon. Use when asked to control an app, tab, or Mac system state, keep the Mac awake, or write a Hammerspoon module. Not for web page content.

skills.name: html-lesson
skills.description: Turn a paper, notebook, chapter, or design doc into a narrated, self-paced HTML lesson — one self-contained file with chapters, subtitles, worked numbers, pause-and-predict questions, and optional TTS narration; the finished lesson can also be filmed into one MP4. Use when asked for a tutorial/teaching video "as HTML", an explainer or lesson for a source, or to preview/teach a topic in finance, RL/ML, or distributed systems. Do NOT use for an in-chat diagram (use show-me), a chart of real data (use dataviz), a single illustration (use sketch-concept), a post or explorer showing how your own system's mechanism works (use mechanism-viz), or animation-first math video (this is not Manim).
skills.compatibility: uv (scripts run as uv scripts, Python 3.10+); node for evaluating the lesson script (22 or newer for `video`); Chromium or Chrome for the per-beat check, screenshots and `video`; ffmpeg for narration and `video`; an OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech endpoint for narration (optional); asr.py downloads a Whisper model on first run.

skills.name: karpathy-planning
skills.description: Develop a scoped implementation plan when explicitly asked to plan a coding task. Use grill-me for a deliberate design interview.

skills.name: maintain-formal-verification-skill
skills.description: Brings a project's formal verification back in line with the code after the code changes, and says whether each failure is drift in the verification or a bug in the code. Use for /maintain-formal-verification-skill, "is the model still true to the code", or after merges and refactors that touched verified code without rechecking it. Do NOT use to create the first verification (use create-formal-verification-skill).

skills.name: mechanism-viz
skills.description: Plan and build a trace-grounded explanation of how a mechanism in your own system works, as a post with animated figures, an interactive explorer that replays one real instance, and benchmark charts. Use when writing a deep-dive or launch post for your own system, or visualizing how a request, lock, scheduler, cache, protocol, storage engine, or concurrent data structure behaves step by step. Do NOT use for a narrated lesson built from someone else's source (use html-lesson), an in-chat diagram (use show-me), a single illustration (use sketch-concept), a demo of a proposed state model (use state-prototype), or a standalone chart (use dataviz).

skills.name: obsidian-capture
skills.description: Append todos, logs, learnings, and reflections to Obsidian daily or weekly notes and run the agent-todo queue via scripts/capture.py. Use when asked to add a todo, note something down, log this, capture an idea, set a due date, record a weekly reflection, or list or close the agent's tasks ("看你的 todo", "干活"). Not for searching notes (use obsidian-search) or standalone long-form notes.

skills.name: obsidian-search
skills.description: Search an Obsidian vault for topics, exact text, tags, recent notes, and tasks. Use when fuzzy, date-aware, due, or overdue note retrieval is needed.

skills.name: paper-search
skills.description: Find and rank research papers by relevance, recency, field-adjusted impact, venue, and author affiliation. Use when searching AI, agents, runtimes, storage, databases, infrastructure, recent or superseding work, company or lab research, or evidence for technical claims. Do NOT use for general web search or GitHub repository evaluation.

skills.name: readback
skills.description: Put a long reply of your own - or a plan, document, or session transcript - on an HTML page the user reads, highlights, and comments on, returning their notes as a follow-up prompt through a waiting local command. Use when your answer is too long to review in a terminal, when the user wants to mark up or annotate a document, or when you want line-level feedback on a plan before implementing it. Do NOT use to collect answers to specific open decisions or to interview the user one question at a time (use grill-me).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.10+, stdlib only. Live delivery needs a browser on the same machine and a harness that can hold a foreground command open.

skills.name: repo-eval
skills.description: Evaluate a public GitHub repository's momentum and maintenance health. Use when asked whether a repository is healthy, growing, declining, abandoned, or well maintained, or when vetting dependencies and OSS projects. Do NOT use for code or architecture review.

skills.name: route-skill
skills.description: Discovers skills in the wilbeibi-skills catalog and loads explicitly selected skills from local files or cache, fetching missing skills. Use when asked to use an unavailable skill by name, find a suitable skill, or when available capabilities are insufficient and a catalog skill could fill the specific gap. Do NOT treat a question about a skill as permission to use it.
skills.compatibility: Python 3.10+; network access only for uncached catalog entries or skills and explicit refreshes.

skills.name: sherlock
skills.description: Work an open question like a case — graded clues, competing theories in a consistency matrix, eliminate by evidence, backtrack, converge, with a casebook on disk for long cases. Use for puzzling bugs, reverse-engineering how a product works from public signals, or "what actually happened here". Do NOT use for planning (use karpathy-planning), repo tours (use grok-repo), or diff review.

skills.name: show-me
skills.description: Explain code structure, dataflow, or proposed changes with a compact tree, pseudocode, type signature, diff, or diagram. Use when a visual clarifies those relationships; whole-repo briefings belong to grok-repo.

skills.name: sketch-concept
skills.description: Draw a hand-drawn SVG illustration that explains one technical mechanism or data insight — architecture, concurrency, storage, caching, queues, retries — for a blog post, doc, or slide. Use when asked for an illustration, a hand-drawn or Excalidraw-style visual, or a picture that makes one engineering idea click. Do NOT use for answering in-chat with a text diagram (use show-me), for charts of real data (use dataviz), or for an animated or interactive step-by-step walkthrough of your own system (use mechanism-viz).
skills.compatibility: Python 3.10+, stdlib only; Chromium or Chrome for `sketch.py check`.

skills.name: skill-curator
skills.description: Audit a skill library for duplicated guidance, contradictions, bloat, dead references, and defects. Use when cleaning, consolidating, or de-duplicating a skills tree.

skills.name: state-prototype
skills.description: Builds a throwaway single-file HTML demo of a proposed state model, driven by an explicit transition table, with free-play buttons and scenario tabs a person can click through. Use when asked to prototype, sanity-check, or feel out a state machine, lifecycle, or status design before implementing it. Do NOT use to explain an existing mechanism (use mechanism-viz), to check every interleaving (use tla-model), to chart a checked model (use statechart), or for a static diagram (use show-me).

skills.name: statechart
skills.description: Checks a TLA+ model of a system that moves between states, such as a product flow, a protocol, or a service lifecycle, and draws it as a Mermaid statechart in the reader's words, with the shortest path to each state that breaks a rule. Use for /statechart, to show a TLC counterexample as a path through states, or to chart a checked model for a reviewer. Do NOT use for a proposed design with no model (use state-prototype) or a hand-drawn diagram (use show-me).

skills.name: test-writing
skills.description: Writes, reviews, and prunes tests so the committed suite protects contracts and invariants rather than implementation. Use when writing or reviewing tests, choosing a test seam, scope, or mocks, adding property, fuzz, or regression tests, fixing brittle tests, auditing a bloated suite, or deciding whether a failing test means the code or the test is wrong. Do NOT use for TLA+ model checking (use tla-model).

skills.name: tla-model
skills.description: Models concurrent and distributed designs in TLA+ or PlusCal and checks them with the TLC model checker. Use when asked to write, review, or debug a TLA+ spec, .tla/.cfg files, or TLC output, or to model-check or formally verify a protocol, lock, lease, consensus, replication, WAL, retry, or race condition. Do NOT use for unit or property-based tests (use test-writing), a click-through demo of a proposed state model (use state-prototype), a reader's chart of a checked model (use statechart), a verify skill kept in a repo (use create-formal-verification-skill), or Lean, Coq, Dafny, or Verus proofs.
skills.compatibility: uv (scripts/tlc.py runs as a uv script, Python 3.10+, no dependencies); Java 11+ and tla2tools.jar (scripts/tlc.py fetch downloads it).

skills.name: wait-what
skills.description: Re-pitches the agent's last message after it did not land, with context first, every label explained, and plain short sentences. Use when the user types /wait-what or says the last message was unclear.

skills.name: web-recap
skills.description: Search browser history for URLs by topic or visit statistics. Use when asked about visited sites, browsing history, or recent online activity. Do NOT use for project/git recaps or agent-session history.

skills.name: write-docs
skills.description: Write or critique prose that ships with a codebase — READMEs, guides and runbooks, CLI help and error text, code comments, AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, commit messages, PR titles and descriptions, and changelog entries. Use when drafting or editing these, including commits and PRs written as part of another task. Do NOT use to review the code in a PR (use code-review), or for blog posts (blog-review), design docs (grill-me), ADRs or glossaries (domain-modeling), or skills (write-skill).

skills.name: write-skill
skills.description: Author or update compact agent skills under skills/<name>/SKILL.md. Use when asked to write, add, or change a skill; not to audit a skill library.
